Cell 5 crashes with: `TypeError: only integer scalar arrays can be converted to a scalar index`

for images, labels in train_ds.take(1):
  for i in range(6):
    ax = plt.subplot(3, 3, i + 1)
    plt.imshow(images[i].numpy().astype("uint8"))
    plt.title(class_names[labels[i]])
    plt.axis("off")
```

The issue is with `class_names[labels[i]]`. The problem is that `labels[i]` is a one-hot encoded array (because `label_mode='categorical'` is used in cell 2), not a scalar integer index.

When using `label_mode='categorical'`, the labels are one-hot encoded tensors/vectors. To get the class index, we need to convert from one-hot encoding to a scalar index. We can use `tf.argmax(labels[i])` or `np.argmax(labels[i].numpy())` to get the index.

Let me fix cell 5:

```python

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))
for images, labels in train_ds.take(1):
  for i in range(6):
    ax = plt.subplot(3, 3, i + 1)
    plt.imshow(images[i].numpy().astype("uint8"))
    plt.title(class_names[tf.argmax(labels[i]).numpy()])
    plt.axis("off")
```

This should fix the error by converting the one-hot encoded label to an index using `tf.argmax`.
